title: Cymatics experiment in the King's Chamber produces the Eye of Horus
summary: Jay Anderson tells of Cymatics experiment in the King's Chamber produces the Eye of Horus, about unspecified at Egypt (no place named), and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: actually um did some experiments alongside some other scientists in the king's chamber where they they stretched a membrane uh over the uh sarcophagus of the king's chamber like a cladney plate like a simatic plate and they put Egyptian sand on the plate and they sent vibrational frequencies that match the the frequency of the king's chamber through it and it turned into the eye of Horus.

plain: A researcher named Jay Anderson, on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, relays an experiment he credits to an author, David Elkington, and other scientists in the King's Chamber, the inner room of Egypt's Great Pyramid. He says they stretched a membrane over the stone box in the chamber, scattered Egyptian sand on it the way you do to make sound vibrations visible, and played frequencies matching the chamber's own tone. According to him, the sand formed the Eye of Horus, an ancient Egyptian symbol, which would suggest the builders designed the pyramid around sound and meaning.
